Manifold

MAN-uh-fohld -- stress on the first syllable, MAN. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Manifold is numerous and various.

The principal's manifold duties ranged from approving budgets to judging the fourth-grade science fair.

Worked Example

In one afternoon, the park ranger repairs a trail sign, rescues a lost hiker, tests the lake water, files a wildfire report, and teaches a class of scouts to read a compass.

The ranger's responsibilities are manifold -- not just numerous but strikingly varied, spanning many different kinds of work. Manifold describes things that are many and diverse at the same time.

How Manifold Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

diverse

diverse: of many different kinds

numerous

numerous: existing in large numbers

multifarious

multifarious: of many and various types

Antonyms

identical

identical: exactly alike

few

few: small in number

How Strong Is It? — numerous → manifold → multifarious

numerous vs. manifold

numerous vs. manifold: Numerous counts heads and nothing more, so it is weaker than manifold -- numerous complaints are simply many, while manifold complaints are many and of many different kinds.

multifarious vs. manifold

multifarious vs. manifold: Multifarious out-varies even manifold: manifold duties are numerous and varied, while multifarious ones sprawl across so many unrelated categories that no single person could sort them.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — mani-/manig

root — mani-/manig: many (Old English manig)

suffix — -fold

suffix — -fold: times, ways (Old English -feald)

Put it together

Put it together: Manifold is pure Old English: manig ('many') plus -fold ('times, ways') -- literally 'many ways.' Things that are manifold do not just come in large numbers; they come in many different kinds, folded together from every direction.

Use the root in a new word: tenfold

Use the root in a new word: tenfold: Ticket sales grew tenfold once the video went viral.

Word Choice

Manifold is a formal, slightly literary adjective that sits before plural nouns: manifold reasons, manifold challenges, manifold blessings. Choose it when you mean many AND varied -- if the items are all of one kind, plain 'many' is the honest word.
